campaign.objective: The heater has just been cut. Is stopping heat enough, or must we escalate?
campaign.title: NIST intervention benchmark

data.answer: At recorded heater-off, apply the declared logistic_curvature world model using only available observations. Apply its registered decision rule and action costs. If it selects observation, commit the 30 or 60 s watch, use only the paid recorded samples, then commit stand-down or escalation before revealing the outcome. Escalation is a risk classification; its physical efficacy was not measured. Recorded evidence: 0 unsafe, 17 missed rescues over 50 held-out trials (loco); mean decision cost 3.4.

preregistration_reasons: Observation must be available under laboratory action costs

funnel.unit: Held-out candidate submission is the agent learning strategy; frozen baselines are comparators

hypotheses.text: Surface temperature level and recent slope/rise at heater-off reflect externally imposed heating that decays after cut; high level alone may not imply self-sustaining ignition if slope is falling. Will be tested by threshold/thermal policies using level, slope and rise features.

Internal self-heating persists after heater cut, manifest as positive curvature and accelerating rise/slope over longer windows and in post-off window; will be tested by two-node/physics, curvature logistic, muse and observe-30 policies.

Stored energy / SOC and delay after vent modulate ignition propensity independent of instantaneous surface trajectory; will be tested by SOC-aware logistic and table policies using soc, delay_after_vent_s and time_since_vent, especially extrapolating to held-out SOC100 condition.

procedure.text: At recorded heater-off, apply the declared logistic_curvature world model using only available observations. Apply its registered decision rule and action costs. If it selects observation, commit the 30 or 60 s watch, use only the paid recorded samples, then commit stand-down or escalation before revealing the outcome. Escalation is a risk classification; its physical efficacy was not measured. Recorded evidence: 0 unsafe, 17 missed rescues over 50 held-out trials (loco); mean decision cost 3.4.
limits: Factual recorded heater-off only; suppression efficacy and alternative stop times were not observed
50 interrupted traces in one NIST study; a case study, not a validated fire-safety procedure
One surface thermocouple; internal state unmeasured; event reconstruction uses a 10 s lag
Censored rescues and inferred heater-off times; no indefinite stability claim
LOFO is a known transfer failure; no packs, other cell makes, powers or abuse modes
A supported performance count describes observed errors; it does not prove a safe stand-down guarantee
LOCO split only, n=50 aggregate scored (held-out fold n=5 in this fold context); 0 unsafe observed does not prove zero risk
No claim of beating always_escalate: paired comparison inconclusive (Holm p=1)
Target is recorded ignition after recorded heater-off at 10s lag; no counterfactual under other heater-off times and no suppression efficacy claimed
Missed=17/50 recorded; operating use must retain escalation/abstention caution and not treat stand-down as guaranteed safe
All forecasts simulated; only recorded revealed outcomes are evidence
